intent: Close the race where batcher.Commit passes the closed-check and then enqueues its request behind Shutdown's quit marker, which made sync callers hang forever and silently dropped async uploads. A mutex now makes Commit's closed-check plus send one step, and Shutdown's close(closed) plus quit-marker send one step. Late commits still get the 'batcher is shutting down' error, and a deterministic regression test is added.
residual_risks: Commit holds admitMu across a blocking send on b.in (lib/batcher/batcher.go:276). If b.in is full while a slow batch commit runs, Shutdown waits on the mutex before it closes b.closed. The total wait matches the old code, where the quit send itself blocked, but Commits already queued on the mutex are admitted and committed rather than rejected. Nothing can deadlock because commitLoop keeps draining b.in until it reads the quit marker, and no CommitBatchFn calls back into Commit or Shutdown. That caller check used grep only, over backend/dropbox and backend/googlephotos.
testing_gaps: The regression test uses Size 1 with a single committer, so it never covers Shutdown contending with a Commit that holds admitMu while blocked on a full b.in (more concurrent committers than Size, during a slow CommitBatchFn). That lock-held-across-send path is where a future deadlock would appear.
